stories.title: Many women have never discussed heart health with a clinician, and most report multiple symptoms
stories.summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, and the risk rises during the menopause years. But an international study has revealed that only half of women know this. Many have never talked about their heart with a doctor or a nurse, and the majority are living with multiple symptoms.

stories.title: Cold Triggers a Hidden Molecular Pathway That Extends Lifespan, Study Finds
stories.summary: Can we harness this? ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.

stories.title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say
stories.summary: Chomping on vegtable skins, seeds and stalks could give us vital fibre, say food scientists.

stories.title: The parts of fruits and vegetables most throw away could save your health—and the planet
stories.summary: Most of us routinely discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at mealtime. But new research from King's College London suggests these scraps could be a valuable—and overlooked—source of dietary fiber, offering potential benefits for both public health and the environment.

stories.title: Manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, say UK experts
stories.summary: Report calls for an effort to tackle harms in similar way to obesity and smoking, and stresses need to ‘offer boys something better’ The manosphere and online misogyny should be treated by the government as a public health issue, in the same way as obesity or smoking, experts have said.

stories.title: Could a few bad dietary choices worsen your next immune response?
stories.summary: Scientists have long known that diet shapes the immune system. Now, a UC San Francisco team has found that even a brief dietary change can substantially change how the body responds to skin irritation, at least in mice.

stories.title: When things go bump in the night: How our brains trick us into hearing things that aren't there
stories.summary: It's 3 a.m. You've woken from a dead sleep because you've heard a thud in the darkness or a floorboard creaking downstairs. Or perhaps you've woken because you have the unmistakable sensation you're not alone.

stories.title: Tumor mutations and immune activity may reveal who benefits from investigational lymphoma drug
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba conducted a physician-initiated phase 2 clinical trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T-follicular helper cell lymphoma (TFHL), an aggressive and difficult-to-treat blood cancer.

stories.title: Heat waves and pollution increase stroke risk in older adults, study finds
stories.summary: A study conducted in Brazil by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) found that each additional day spent under a heat wave in São Paulo is associated with an increased risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older.

stories.title: Healthy diet may lower heart disease risk after cancer
stories.summary: Eating a healthy diet is associated with a reduced risk of heart disease and death among cancer survivors, according to a study published today in JACC: Advances.

stories.title: Antibody candidate could help preserve appetite and muscle strength in patients with cancer
stories.summary: In cancer cachexia, patients continue to lose weight, muscle and fat even when they eat. A KAIST research team has developed a therapeutic candidate that blocks a signal responsible for appetite suppression, weight loss and excessive energy expenditure.

stories.title: STI screening linked to fewer preterm births
stories.summary: Screening and treating pregnant patients for three common sexually transmitted infections (STIs) twice during pregnancy was associated with a 23% lower risk of preterm birth compared with standard care, according to a randomized clinical trial published in Clinical Infectious Diseases from…

stories.title: Vitamin-carrying protein pathway shows promise for brain drug delivery
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland have identified a transporter protein with the potential to open new avenues for improving creatine delivery into the brain and for developing other therapies targeting the central nervous system.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a new policy for compounding peptides, a PBM disclosure rule, and more
stories.summary: HHS released a policy that will temporarily allow compounding pharmacies to manufacture some peptide products

stories.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test -- and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it.

stories.title: NHS Western Isles prescribing weight loss drugs at triple the rate of other health boards
stories.summary: A new report finds "significant variation" between Scotland's health boards prescribing new medicines.

stories.title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered a small group of brain cells that prevents dangerous blood pressure swings, even when average readings appear normal. The finding reveals a hidden source of cardiovascular risk and could open the door to new treatments that protect the heart and brain.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about 340B battles, new results for a Lilly weight loss drug, and more
stories.summary: Missouri attorney general warned Eli Lilly to discontinue requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under 340B program

stories.title: STAT+: Lilly’s triple-G drug beats Ozempic in head-to-head study
stories.summary: Eli Lilly announced that its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic in a large diabetes study.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden reason why muscles weaken with age
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden defense mechanism in aging muscles that sacrifices strength to protect cells from damage.

stories.title: ‘Ferritin face’: are social media claims about iron deficiency fact – or fiction?
stories.summary: Experts say symptoms such as dark circles under the eyes, grey skin, cracked lips and hair loss can be a warning sign – but there are other factors too TikTok is rife with influencers warning of “ferritin face”, a term they use to describe the pallor, dark circles, dry skin, and hair loss claimed…

stories.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
stories.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain.

stories.title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
stories.summary: The secret to aging more slowly may be hiding in your gut. Scientists discovered that certain gut bacteria are strongly linked to how quickly the body ages, with microbial differences accounting for about 15% of the variation in biological aging rates.

stories.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.

stories.title: The surprisingly simple exercise that could lower your blood pressure
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple exercise routine could help lower blood pressure without requiring daily workouts or expensive equipment.

stories.title: Exercise doesn't just strengthen your heart. It rewires it
stories.summary: Regular exercise does more than strengthen the heart. New research reveals that it actually reshapes the nerves controlling how the heart functions, and the changes are surprisingly different on the left and right sides of the body.

stories.title: Scientists reveal the hidden danger of missing blood pressure medication
stories.summary: Missing blood pressure medication could mean losing much of its protection against heart attacks and strokes, according to an analysis of more than 91,000 people.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
stories.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.

stories.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging.

stories.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
stories.summary: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure. In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated.

stories.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
stories.summary: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s
stories.summary: A seven-year study found that people with Parkinson’s disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities.

stories.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
stories.summary: The scientists involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.

stories.title: Give more people weight-loss jabs on the NHS, say MPs
stories.summary: Current plans for 6% of eligible patients to get Mounjaro by 2028 unambitious, say MPs.

stories.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
stories.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates. The secret lies in subtle changes to brain-building cells that slow neuron production, revealing new clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved.

stories.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates.

stories.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
stories.summary: Drugs will be tested simultaneously, which it's hoped will speed up the process of finding new treatments for this common type of dementia.

stories.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
stories.summary: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight.

stories.title: Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
stories.summary: A new Penn State study suggests that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults.

stories.title: Scientists find 10 different diets linked to slower aging
stories.summary: A study by DZNE finds that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging—and that there is more than one way to eat healthily.

stories.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage.

stories.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
stories.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
stories.summary: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers.

stories.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
stories.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early…

stories.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

stories.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
stories.summary: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical…

stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
stories.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.

stories.title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a potential new drug can reverse severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and blocking harmful substances from reaching the liver.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.

stories.title: Yale scientists discover how stress changes the brain to make memories stronger
stories.summary: Yale scientists have uncovered how the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories.

stories.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
stories.summary: Popular diabetes and weight loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss.

stories.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength
stories.summary: A 47-year study has uncovered a surprising turning point in physical aging: fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among people who exercise regularly.

stories.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults, and scientists can't fully explain why
stories.summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved.

stories.title: Decade-long gym steroids study shows just what happens to men's hearts
stories.summary: One of the first long-term studies that followed weight-training middle-aged men for nearly a decade has found that consistent use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) leads to the thickening of the heart’s left ventricular wall, which increasingly reduces the organ's ability to function.

stories.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
stories.summary: Ice baths, massages, compression garments, and recovery supplements promise faster muscle recovery, but research suggests their benefits are often overstated, and some techniques may even undermine long-term gains.

stories.title: Scientists discover how harmful “zombie cells” hide from the immune system
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a protein that may help harmful aging cells hide from the immune system, allowing them to accumulate and fuel age-related health problems.

stories.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
stories.summary: Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological…

stories.title: After 30 years, scientists finally have a drug for a deadly brain disease
stories.summary: The FDA has approved the first drug that directly targets Alexander disease, a devastating neurological disorder affecting fewer than one in a million people.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden problem with endless smartphone scrolling
stories.summary: Excessive smartphone use may be taking a hidden toll on the brain and body, with heavy scrolling linked to poorer memory, reduced attention, disrupted sleep, and potential balance problems.

stories.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days.

stories.title: Just 10 minutes of daily exercise could unlock deeper sleep
stories.summary: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently experienced more deep, restorative sleep, which is essential for brain recovery, memory, and emotional well-being.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.

stories.title: Eating olive oil before carbs has a surprising effect on blood sugar
stories.summary: A simple change in the order you eat your food could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists discovered that giving mice olive oil before carbohydrates slowed digestion and activated a surprising combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, even in mice with type…

stories.title: A surprisingly simple way to relieve knee arthritis pain without pills or surgery
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple change in how you walk could help relieve knee arthritis pain and even slow joint damage. In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without…

stories.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat and keep muscle
stories.summary: A six-month study suggests that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) may offer older adults a powerful advantage: losing body fat while keeping their muscle.

stories.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
stories.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect.

stories.title: FDA-approved epilepsy drug may help reverse osteoarthritis damage
stories.summary: Researchers at Yale have identified a promising new approach to osteoarthritis that could do more than simply ease pain. The epilepsy drug lacosamide appears to block a protein involved in both pain signaling and cartilage destruction, helping damaged joints shift back toward repair in preclinical…

stories.title: Goodbye joint replacements? Stanford scientists found a way to regrow cartilage and stop arthritis
stories.summary: Scientists have found a surprising way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age.

stories.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
stories.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

stories.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
stories.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood.

stories.title: This common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
stories.summary: High-dose vitamin B3 is showing intriguing early promise as an addition to standard glioblastoma treatment, with 82% of patients in a small trial remaining progression-free after six months.

stories.title: Vitamin D drug may help crack pancreatic cancer’s protective shield
stories.summary: A vitamin D analog may help break down pancreatic cancer’s protective defenses, potentially making tumors more vulnerable to chemotherapy and immune attack. A small clinical trial found encouraging responses, especially in patients whose tumors had high levels of the vitamin D receptor.

stories.title: Diet drinks work as well as water for weight loss, major trial finds
stories.summary: A two-year randomized clinical trial involving 493 adults with overweight or obesity found that diet soft drinks were essentially as effective as water for long-term weight loss and weight maintenance.

stories.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
stories.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

stories.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

stories.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
stories.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.
